intent: The popup of a Combobox, portalled and positioned against its field, holding the list and the no-results message.
typical_uses: The popup that holds a combobox's ComboboxList and ComboboxEmpty

dont_use_when.situation: A fixed list of options with no typed query
A floating panel with arbitrary content, not tied to a filterable field

invariants.text: The popup is in the DOM only while the combobox is open or animating closed; the kit passes no `keepMounted` to the portal, so a closed combobox renders no popup.

Without `container`, the popup portals into the node of the nearest enclosing portal, or the document body when there is none; a theme scoped to a subtree reaches the popup only when that subtree, or a node inside it, is passed as `container`.

Without `anchor`, the popup is placed against the combobox's input element; combobox.module.css makes it as wide as that anchor (at least 9rem) and no taller than the space available, and the list inside it scrolls.
The popup fades and scales on open and close; under `prefers-reduced-motion` combobox.module.css drops the transform transition and keeps the fade.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave out `anchor` in a combobox whose field is ComboboxChips
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass the ref from `useComboboxAnchor()` both to ComboboxChips and to this `anchor`, so the popup lines up with the whole chips field rather than with the inline input among the chips

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the popup portals into; an explicit null renders no popup until a node is passed
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

anchor.states: anchor is the element, virtual element, ref or function returning one that the popup is placed against
anchor.because: `Element | VirtualElement | RefObject<Element | null> | (() => Element | VirtualElement | null) | null` - live DOM nodes, refs and functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

sideOffset.states: sideOffset is the gap in pixels between the anchor and the popup, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
sideOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

alignOffset.states: alignOffset is the shift in pixels along the alignment axis, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
alignOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

collisionBoundary.states: collisionBoundary is the area the popup is kept inside, `clipping-ancestors`, an element, a list of elements or a rectangle
collisionBoundary.because: `'clipping-ancestors' | Element | Element[] | Rect` mixes a string with live DOM elements, which no JSON Schema type covers.

collisionPadding.states: collisionPadding is the space in pixels kept from the collision boundary, one number or a per-side object
collisionPadding.because: `number | { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

initialFocus.states: initialFocus decides what receives focus when the popup opens - false for nothing, true for the default, a ref, or a function of the interaction type
initialFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType) => boolean | void | HTMLElement | null)` mixes a boolean with refs and functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

finalFocus.states: finalFocus decides what receives focus when the popup closes - false for nothing, true for the default, a ref, or a function of the interaction type
finalFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType) => boolean | void | HTMLElement | null)` mixes a boolean with refs and functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the popup's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the popup's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, side, align, anchorHidden, transitionStatus, empty). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside ComboboxContent; only its `container` is exposed, as ComboboxContent's own prop.
Composed inside ComboboxContent; its placement props are exposed on ComboboxContent itself.

good.title: The list beside a no-results message
good.code:
<Combobox items={regions}>
  <ComboboxInput aria-label="Region" />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No regions found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>

good.title: A popup portalled into a themed subtree

bad.title: Items placed straight into the popup
bad.why: ComboboxContent does not wrap its children in a list, so these items sit in no listbox and the list's padding and scrolling are lost; put them inside ComboboxList.
